record.paper_title: The puzzle of global Double Field Theory: open problems and the case for a Higher Kaluza-Klein perspective
record.original_question: Can Double Field Theory recover a general geometric string background, meaning a smooth spacetime manifold equipped with a non-trivial Kalb-Ramond field whose Dixmier-Douady class [H] is nonzero in H3(M, Z), rather than only the restricted cases in which the recovered gerbe is flat or torsion?

evidence.quote: Open problem. Therefore it does not seem possible to recover a general geometric string background made of a smooth manifold M equipped with a non-trivial Kalb-Ramond field [H] ∈ H3(M, Z). And, since DFT was introduced to extend supergravity, the impossibility of recovering supergravity poses a problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In string theory a geometric string background consists of a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a closed 3-form $H \in \Omega^3(M)$ with integral periods, representing the curvature of a $U(1)$-bundle gerbe whose Dixmier–Douady class $[H] \in H^3(M,\mathbb{Z})$ classifies the gerbe up to isomorphism. The Kalb–Ramond $B$-field is a (local) connective structure on this gerbe; globally, on overlapping patches it is glued by gauge transformations governed by the gerbe data.

Double Field Theory (DFT) is a field theory formulated on a "doubled" space whose local model is $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$ with coordinates $(x^\mu, \tilde x_\mu)$ subject to the strong constraint $\partial^M \otimes \partial_M = 0$, with an $O(d,d)$-invariant generalized metric $\mathcal{H}_{MN}$ encoding the metric $g$ and the $B$-field. Solutions of the strong constraint locally depend on only $d$ of the $2d$ coordinates, recovering an ordinary $d$-dimensional supergravity background $(g, B)$.

Question. Does there exist a globally defined formulation of Double Field Theory that, upon solving the strong constraint, recovers an arbitrary geometric string background $(M, [H])$ with smooth manifold $M$ and topologically non-trivial Kalb–Ramond field having Dixmier–Douady class $[H] \neq 0$ in $H^3(M,\mathbb{Z})$ (in particular, classes that are neither zero nor torsion)? Equivalently, can the patching/glueing data of DFT be extended so that the recovered bundle gerbe is allowed to have arbitrary, non-flat, non-torsion Dixmier–Douady class, rather than only the cases in which the gerbe is flat or torsion?
artifact.category_tag: Double Field Theory and bundle gerbes
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on extended/higher geometric formulations of Double Field Theory (e.g., Alfonsi's program on the higher Kaluza–Klein/extended correspondence) discusses this as an unresolved problem: a global DFT geometry that recovers an arbitrary Kalb–Ramond field with non-trivial Dixmier–Douady class is not known. Proposals interpret doubled geometry as an atlas for the higher geometry of bundle gerbes, but a complete construction recovering general non-flat, non-torsion gerbes from DFT remains open.

status_evidence.title: Towards an extended/higher correspondence
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses globalisation of DFT and proposes an interpretation of doubled geometry as atlas for bundle gerbes, addressing the unresolved problem of recovering non-trivial Dixmier–Douady classes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of recovering general non-trivial gerby Kalb–Ramond fields from DFT is treated as still-open and motivates a higher geometric reformulation.

status_evidence.title: L. Alfonsi, Global Double Field Theory and Higher Kaluza-Klein
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews open problems in global DFT including the inability to recover supergravity backgrounds with non-trivial Dixmier–Douady class.
status_evidence.claim: Recovery of arbitrary geometric string backgrounds with [H] non-zero in H^3(M,Z) from DFT is identified as an open problem.
